questions.stem: Why are biological specimens often stained before being viewed under a light microscope?

options.text: Staining adds colour and contrast, making cell structures easier to see
Staining is required to keep the cells alive during observation
Staining makes the microscope magnify the specimen more
Staining increases the resolution of the microscope

questions.explanation: Most cell structures are transparent or nearly colourless. Staining adds colour and contrast to specific structures, making them visible and easier to distinguish under the microscope.
